draft.emotion: a sharp, bitter tone, reflecting a sense of inner resentment
notes: Takes عَلَى ('alā) for the person or thing one is possessive over, and مِن (min) for the person one envies or sees as a rival.
As an adjective on the فَعُول (fa'ūl) pattern, it stays غَيُور for both masculine and feminine singular in formal Arabic (though غَيُورَة is common in everyday speech).

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy, protective, or possessive because someone you love might be interested in others, or because someone else has what you want.

examples.text: لَا تَكُنْ غَيُورًا جِدًّا عَلَى شَرِيكِ حَيَاتِكَ.
examples.translation: Do not be overly jealous and possessive of your life partner.
He is jealous of his friend's success.
examples.emotion: a slightly bitter and resentful tone

draftBefore.emotion: a sharp, bitter tone, reflecting a sense of inner resentment
notes: While 'ghayur' often refers to protectiveness or romantic jealousy, it also captures the feeling of envy when someone else has something you desire.
It is a strong, permanent adjective describing someone's character rather than a fleeting emotion.

senses.definition: Feeling unhappy or possessive because you think someone you love might be interested in someone else.

examples.text: لا تَكُنْ غَيُورًا جِدًّا عَلَى شَرِيكِ حَيَاتِكَ.

faults.quote: Feeling unhappy or angry because you want what someone else has.
faults.why: Oversplit senses, and puts envy first; غَيُور primarily means romantically/protectively jealous (حَسُود is envious).

faults.quote: Do not be too jealous of your life partner.
faults.why: غَيُور عَلَى means 'jealous/possessive over' a partner, whereas English 'jealous of' means envying them.
Needs to explain the prepositions (عَلَى for protective/romantic jealousy, مِن for jealousy toward a rival) and invariant gender.
